claims.text: A DR drill destroys an environment on purpose and rebuilds it by the written steps, timed, to find what the steps miss before a real disaster does.

The Git server (Gitea, Deployment gitea in namespace git) runs inside donhang-staging and keeps its repositories in the cluster, so they are lost with it; dr-drill.sh:25-28 says the mirror clone is all that comes back and later commits are lost.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3 scripts/devops/dr-drill.sh:25-30; deploy/gitops/git-server.yaml (storage); STAGE.md Clusters

claims.text: dr-drill.sh:30-40: if Deployment gitea runs, the script replaces $config_mirror with a fresh git clone --mirror; else it uses an existing mirror; with neither it exits 1. $config_mirror is .gitops/donhang-config.git (scripts/lib/gitops.sh).
git clone --mirror copies all refs (every branch and tag) of the remote into a bare repository; git push --mirror pushes all refs under refs/ to the remote.
The disaster (dr-drill.sh:48-50) runs tofu-env.sh staging platform destroy, then cluster destroy, both with -auto-approve; the clock starts on the next line (51, drill_started=$SECONDS).
OpenTofu's -auto-approve option makes destroy (like apply) skip its interactive approval of the plan and run without stopping to ask.
claims.source_hint: OpenTofu docs: Command: apply, -auto-approve; Command: destroy

claims.text: Two OpenTofu layers: cluster (creates cluster donhang-staging) and platform (namespace donhang, Secret sealing-key). Rebuild (dr-drill.sh:53-77): tofu-env.sh staging up (cluster, then platform), Sealed Secrets then Argo CD, Git server + mirror push, the Application.
After applying the Application, dr-drill.sh (line 100, outside the excerpts) waits until it is Synced and Healthy; the captured output ends step 4 with 'staging: Synced, Healthy'.

The platform module (deploy/tofu/modules/donhang-platform/main.tf) has two resources: namespace donhang and Secret sealing-key in kube-system, type kubernetes.io/tls, from var.sealing_certificate/var.sealing_private_key, label sealedsecrets.bitnami.com/sealed-secrets-key=active.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3 deploy/tofu/modules/donhang-platform/main.tf:17-41; output 'Plan: 2 to add' in dr-drill.txt

claims.text: The Sealed Secrets controller (in kube-system, controller.yaml) loads as its keys the Secrets in its namespace labeled sealedsecrets.bitnami.com/sealed-secrets-key=active; with key renewal off (--key-renew-period=0) and a key present, it creates none of its own.
claims.source_hint: Sealed Secrets README: Bring your own certificates / key renewal; main.tf:24-27 comment; deploy/sealed-secrets/controller.yaml:13, 45

claims.text: With --without-sealing-key, dr-drill.sh:57-60 deletes Secret sealing-key from kube-system before installing the controller, standing in for a lost secrets/sealing.key.

Recorded output without the key: SealedSecret db condition 'no key could decrypt secret (POSTGRES_PASSWORD)', no Secrets in donhang, db Pod waiting with CreateContainerConfigError, Deployment api NotFound (sync stops at wave 0).
A container whose environment references a Secret that does not exist does not start and the kubelet retries; the recorded run shows the db container waiting with reason CreateContainerConfigError.
claims.source_hint: Kubernetes docs: Secrets (using Secrets as environment variables; missing Secret prevents the container from starting); Debug Pods

claims.text: Argo CD applies sync waves in order and does not apply the next wave until resources of the current wave are healthy, so the api (a later wave) is never applied while wave 0 is not healthy.
claims.source_hint: Argo CD docs: Sync Phases and Waves (how waves work, waits for health)

claims.text: scripts/dev-secrets.sh writes TOFU_STATE_PASSPHRASE to .env (lines 43-50) and the sealing key pair to secrets/ (59-69); its comments say each is in no backup. STAGE.md: nothing under secrets/ is committed.

OpenTofu state stores resource attributes, so the platform state holds a copy of the sealing key Secret's data; the state lives in donhang_tofu on Compose's PostgreSQL (tofu-env.sh), is read before any change, and with encryption enforced cannot be read without its passphrase.
claims.source_hint: OpenTofu docs: State (purpose, sensitive data); State and Plan Encryption (pbkdf2, unrecoverable without key); tofu-env.sh:2-3, 20; envs/staging/platform/backend.tf

claims.text: backup-logical.sh dumps donhang_tofu, the database that holds OpenTofu's state, so its dumps include the encrypted state.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3 scripts/devops/backup-logical.sh (database list); devops.l3.logical-backups outline item 2

claims.text: Staging's db keeps its data in an emptyDir, whose data is deleted when its Pod is removed, so a new db Pod starts from db-init.yaml's seed; the drill restores no database.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3 deploy/gitops/config-repo/envs/staging/db.yaml:2, 63; db-init.yaml:1; Kubernetes docs: Volumes, emptyDir

claims.text: STAGE.md (stage-3): dr-drill.sh rebuilds staging with only the Application apps/staging.yaml; Traefik (the reverse proxy on staging's node ports 30080/30443) and other pieces come back with their own scripts.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3 STAGE.md:137-138; deploy/tofu/envs/staging/cluster/main.tf (Traefik comment); config-repo/apps/traefik.yaml

claims.text: At the end (dr-drill.sh:104-108) the script prints each timed step's seconds and the total from losing the cluster to Healthy; step() and finish_step() record each step's duration with $SECONDS.

The drill's total is staging's measured recovery time for the steps it runs, set against the RTO target; until the missing steps are in the list, it is a lower bound. When it exceeds the target, change the steps or the target, then drill again.
A review of a written recovery plan checks that the steps make sense, not that they finish or how long they take; running them shows that, and often exposes a missing step a review overlooked.

Keeping the sealing key and state passphrase out of the backups they protect is deliberate: a copy inside would let anyone holding a backup read every secret it protects, so they need their own copy on another machine, apart from the backups.

tofu-env.sh runs dev-secrets.sh before OpenTofu; dev-secrets.sh writes a new TOFU_STATE_PASSPHRASE when .env lacks one and a new sealing key pair when secrets/sealing.key is missing. No step of dr-drill.sh reads the key back from OpenTofu's state.

dr-drill.sh step() prints a heading and records the step's start ($SECONDS); gitops.sh git_server_open port-forwards service/gitea to the host, git_server_close stops it, git_auth runs git with the admin's credentials in an Authorization header. Step 3 creates Gitea's admin user and an empty repo.
